Implemented the rest of docs/design/frontend-auth.md §4.6. Two halves:

DENY LIST. Tailnet::deny adds a node, writes it and ticks a watch; identify refuses a denied node before any rule, the listed ones included. The watch is what makes a deny immediate: each tailnet session brings its next recheck forward instead of waiting out recheck_s, so sessions close at once. Kept in tailnet-denied in the state directory, mode 0600, at most MAX_DENIED nodes. /msg mimid tailnet deny <node> is the command; PeerIdentity gained deny, denied and changes so the rules stay in mimid-agent and mimid-agent-irc only asks.

SESSION REGISTRY. mimid-agent-irc's Shared gained a registry of registered connections (peer, node, whether the node let it in, credential, since) with a guard that takes a connection out when it closes. /msg mimid tailnet now lists every node with a connection open and the sessions from it, which is what §4.6 asked for and what the previous version could not do, because connections live in a JoinSet that nothing can enumerate.

TWO CHOICES WORTH KNOWING. (1) The deny list is a FILE, not a table, though §4.6 says the agent's database: it is a short list of names written only by the running daemon, so it needs no transaction and no schema, the tailscale cert consent of §5.2 already sits beside it in the same shape, and it keeps the feature inside mimid-agent instead of needing a new mimid-agent-store table. (2) There is NO UNDENY command: the file is edited instead. An undeny typed from a client that the denied node may be holding is a way back in, which is the one thing a deny list exists to stop.

Test: tests/tailnet.rs a_denied_node_loses_its_sessions_and_stays_denied covers two sessions from one node, the listing counting both, a deny closing both including the asking one, a new connection from that node falling back to the password rules and being refused, and the denial still in force after a restart. All gates green, full suite with no failures.
